propositions: RP-01 requires resolving all material behavioral differences between Rebar's structured-output orchestration and Pydantic AI 1.107.2 before implementation, with explicit classification of each delta as preserve, intentionally change, or maintainer decision—no silent inheritance.

The offline in-process probe must exercise real Agent/NativeOutput/PromptedOutput/FallbackModel/UsageLimits/Hooks seams with mocked provider transport and report exact observable oracles (call count, exception class, usage fields, telemetry) against 19 deduplicated scenarios derived from 15 historical ticket aliases and existing test suites.

Material historical behaviors must be preserved including deterministic repair, schema/sentinel extraction, three-attempt ceiling, stop-reason fast-fail, derived operation budgets with re-clamping, fallback predicate/order, cumulative usage accounting, bounded final-failure artifact policy, and ordered typed failure taxonomy.

Highest-impact pending decision: whether Pydantic output retries and tool turns share one operation-wide request_limit (consuming a combined allowance) or whether each output retry receives a fresh Agent run with a fresh budget.

Current Rebar truncates only intermediate failed responses at 2,000 characters on retry while preserving full input, accepted output, and final artifact; Pydantic ProcessHistory and prefix truncation risk silent completeness loss in recomputed findings, requiring explicit all-or-nothing policy clarification.

Cache-impact validation with live Anthropic and Bedrock showed same-run retries increase cache reads by 64% and decrease writes by 84% due to prefix reuse; message-tail benefits are provider-specific and require explicit breakpoint configuration even in single_turn mode.
